sections.title: What Is Observation?
sections.transcript: Observation means noticing details carefully. **Start with what you can see.** Keep your description separate from your explanation.
sections.narration_ready: Observation means noticing details carefully. Start with what you can see. Keep your description separate from your explanation.

sections.title: Gather Your Materials
sections.transcript:
Bring these materials:
- A notebook
- A pencil
- A familiar object
You do not need special equipment.
sections.narration_ready: Bring these materials: a notebook, a pencil, and a familiar object. You do not need special equipment.

sections.title: Describe Before Explaining
sections.transcript: Choose an object that you can examine safely, such as a leaf, a spoon, or a piece of fabric. Give yourself a full minute to observe it before writing anything. Notice its shape, its color, and the way light falls across its surface. Then write three sentences that describe only what you observed. A description such as 'the edge is uneven' records a visible detail. An explanation such as 'an insect ate the edge' proposes a cause. Both can be useful, but they do different jobs. Keep the description first so that another learner can check your evidence before considering your explanation.

sections.title: Keep the Evidence
sections.transcript: Record the date (including the year) beside your notes. If you repeat the activity, use the same object and lighting so that the comparison is useful.
sections.narration_ready: Record the date, including the year, beside your notes. If you repeat the activity, use the same object and lighting so that the comparison is useful.

sections.title: Compare Your Notes
sections.transcript: Compare your notes with a partner. Ask: Which details did we both notice? Which details appeared in only one description? Return to the object to check any disagreement.
sections.narration_ready: Compare your notes with a partner. Ask: Which details did we both notice? Which details appeared in only one description? Return to the object to check any disagreement.

sections.title: Reflect and Repeat
sections.transcript: Write one sentence about what you learned. Then choose another object and repeat the activity. Careful observation improves with practice, and your notes help you notice that progress.
